display.title: Episode 314: The Three Loaves of Bread (Parshas Mishpatim-Shekalim)
display.summary_short: Shabbos Mishpatim, Shekalim and Mevarchim Adar explained, and how Shlomo HaMelech showed a puzzled old woman why the wind carried off her last loaf of bread.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi previews a very special Shabbos. It is Parshas Mishpatim, the laws that follow Mattan Torah, a reminder that every mitzvah is done because Hashem commanded it ('v'tzivanu'). It is Shabbos Shekalim, recalling the half-shekel given for the Mishkan and the communal offerings, which we remember today by giving tzedakah to Torah and prayer. And it is Shabbos Mevarchim for Adar, the month of extra joy. After the Hakochainik march, an eight-year-old yeshiva boy recites the Shema. The story, a lesson in emunah and bitachon: an old woman gives two of her three fresh loaves to starving beggars, and then the wind blows the third out to sea. She asks Shlomo HaMelech why. He tells her to trust Hashem, and soon a foreign king arrives: his leaking ship was saved when a loaf of bread plugged the hole, and he had vowed half his wealth to charity. The bread matches hers exactly. The show closes with the Jewish Children's Expo, Shabbos candle time and Dial-a-Jewish-Story.
display.lesson: Everything Hashem does is for the good, even when we cannot yet see why; trust Him and be patient.
